primitives.name: Meshy single-object reconstruction
primitives.verbatim_quote: (Param behavior re-checked against docs.meshy.ai 2026-06-11.) ## Rule 1 — ONE figure per input image (character sheets) Meshy reconstructs **everything in the frame as a single object**.
primitives.assumptions: ['The input image contains exactly one distinct figure.', 'All other elements in the frame are considered part of the target object.']
primitives.breakdown_regime: Geometry collapses into fused components when multiple figures are present.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI conformal prediction intervals for bounding reconstruction uncertainty in multi-camera tracking.
layer2.telemetry: Number of detected semantic segments in the input image

primitives.name: Character sheet fusion anomaly
primitives.verbatim_quote: A character sheet with 4 views becomes "a statuette of 4 fused figures".
primitives.assumptions: ['Figures are positioned adjacently without separation in the sheet.', 'No explicit cropping or segmentation is applied prior to reconstruction.']
primitives.breakdown_regime: Auto-rigging fails due to topological non-manifoldness at fusion seams.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE collision detection for articulated rigid bodies with overlapping bounding volumes.

primitives.name: Single-view reconstruction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Two valid paths: - **One best view** (front or 3/4) → regular `image-to-3d`.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'M_{\\text{single}}': 'Reconstructed mesh (geometric)', 'I_{\\text{best}}': 'Selected optimal view image (dimensionless)', '\\mathcal{R}_{\\text{Meshy}}': 'Operator mapping single-view to 3D (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: ['The chosen view provides sufficient silhouette information for topology recovery.', 'Pose variations across different views are ignored.']
primitives.breakdown_regime: Loss of depth cues leads to ambiguous shape recovery.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI Kalman filtering for state estimation from partial observations.
layer2.telemetry: Visibility consistency score between projected UV coordinates

primitives.name: Multi-view reconstruction
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Each view as its own file** → `multi-image-to-3d` (1–4 images) — better geometry, but ONLY if the pose is identical on all panels.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'M_{\\text{multi}}': 'Reconstructed mesh ensemble (geometric)', 'I_j': 'j-th panel image (dimensionless)', 'P_j': 'Pose parameter vector of j-th view (dimensionless)', 'P_0': 'Reference pose (dimensionless)', '\\mathcal{R}_{\\text{Meshy}}': 'Operator mapping multiple views to 3D (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: ['All panel images share the same intrinsic camera parameters.', 'Object articulation is minimal or absent across views.', 'Geometric alignment is perfect post-reconstruction.']
primitives.breakdown_regime: Pose mismatches introduce stitching artifacts and topological errors.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) for incremental graph optimization.
layer2.telemetry: Average reprojection error across aligned views

Meshy's 'single object' assumption enforces a global connectivity constraint that simplifies the inverse problem but introduces catastrophic failure modes when violated. The transition from single-view to multi-view can be framed as a joint maximum likelihood estimation over latent poses, where the identically posed multi-view case yields a convex energy landscape amenable to gradient descent, while misaligned views lead to non-convexity and local minima. The T-pose normalization acts as an informative prior that reduces the solution space, analogous to applying a regularization term in an inverse rendering pipeline. The rule about limbs being separated from the torso prevents self-intersection penalties that would otherwise bias the reconstruction towards overly compact shapes.
